crit: 'We choose several real-life datasets with highly skewed class distribution to assess the effectiveness of our proposed learning framework on realistic tasks' (Credit Fraud, two KDDCUP-99 pairs, Record Linkage, Payment Simulation); a synthetic 4x4 checkerboard of 16 Gaussian components is used 'to provide more insights of our framework', with the covariance varied to control class overlap and test robustness; Fig. 2 generated Gaussian datasets (disjoint vs overlapped) show that hardness, not IR, reflects task difficulty.
notes: Real data sources are described but no repository is named (no UCI/Kaggle mention), hence 'Other'. Payment Simulation is itself a simulated dataset from an external source, used as distributed (Natural). KDDCUP binarised by the authors as one-vs-one pairs (DOS vs PRB, DOS vs R2L); other classes dropped. Minority named per dataset (frauds, matches, PRB/R2L). GitHub link (footnotes 1 and 4) is for code and extra results, not the derived KDDCUP subsets. Credit Fraud IR printed 578.88:1 equals #Sample/frauds (284,807/492), whereas the Record Linkage and Payment Simulation IRs match majority/minority; copied as printed. Table IV: each real dataset is paired with its own classifier(s) (Table III 'Model' column); SMOTE and Clean results are missing ('---') for all datasets except Credit Fraud. 60/20/20 train/validation/test split.
